meta.title: ISDS Thematic Watcher — how the whole thing works
meta.note: v2.2 (2026-08-03): the fetch relay added to the machine lane — the daily council session has no network of its own, so it asks and a runner answers with a reduction (400 characters, never the document). Machine rows 7-8 hold the relay; the two builder agents move to 9-10, the digest email and site to 9-10, leaving deliverables row 8 clear as the corridor the relay's answer crosses. v2.1 (operator revisions 2026-07-29): Emory naming, per-agent models + training lines, substantive plain language, badge layout fix, Bing News in / Google News retired, delivery legend reworded.

nodes.title: Runs by itself every Monday
nodes.desc: A scheduled timer starts the whole pipeline — nobody has to remember.
nodes.meta: GitHub Actions schedule, set by Emory

nodes.title: Collect everything new
nodes.desc: Pulls this week's listings from all 9 sources above into one pile.

nodes.title: Skip repeats
nodes.desc: A memory file remembers every item ever seen, so nothing is processed twice.

nodes.title: First scoring pass
nodes.desc: Counts legal key-phrases (the three 'rings') for a quick relevance score.

nodes.title: Read the document
nodes.desc: Fetches each promising item and pulls out its single most quotable line.

nodes.title: AI relevance check
nodes.desc: Claude reads each item and scores its relevance to the research question, with reasons.

nodes.title: Quality bar
nodes.desc: Items scoring 40+ enter the digest. Near-misses (25+) may fill a quiet week, always labeled as leads.

nodes.title: Ask for a page to be read
nodes.desc: The daily review session cannot reach the internet at all, so it writes down the address it needs.
evidence: analytics/fetch-requests/README.md: the request format and its rules
nodes.meta: Starts by itself when a request lands

nodes.title: Only a summary comes back
nodes.desc: A separate run reads the page as politely as the weekly run does, then sends back 400 characters — never the page.
evidence: scripts/fetch_relay.py: polite_get, 400-character excerpt, sha256 + byte length
scripts/fetch_relay.py: CONTROL_URL — a failed control voids the whole batch
nodes.meta: If the test link fails, nothing counts

nodes.title: Daily research email
nodes.desc: Each day's meeting record, emailed to Emory with the numbers-of-record banner.

nodes.title: Weekly digest email
nodes.desc: The annotated reading list of this week's finds — sent to Dr. Benavides.

nodes.title: Public website
nodes.desc: The digest archive and methodology, published automatically to the project site.

nodes.title: Research brief email
nodes.desc: The review stages' plain-English interpretation of the week — sent to Dr. Benavides.

nodes.title: Monday review packet
nodes.desc: Emory's Monday briefing: session minutes and grades, workflow ideas, the state of the answer, and claims needing his check.

nodes.title: Daily researcher
nodes.desc: Runs daily: works the open questions, logs every genuinely new sourced insight, plus at most one improvement idea.

nodes.title: Chairman
nodes.desc: Sets the weekly agenda from the open questions and directs where the analyst spends effort.

nodes.title: Analyst
nodes.desc: Interprets the week against the research question with bounded web research; proposes claims with exact quotes.

nodes.title: Systems researcher
nodes.desc: Studies the instrument itself and proposes one sourced improvement at a time.

nodes.title: Editor
nodes.desc: Writes the reader-facing brief. May state as fact only what survived the gates.

nodes.title: Meeting minutes
nodes.desc: The chairman reviews each member's week on the record: status, grades, next steps, escalations to Emory.

nodes.title: The living memory
nodes.desc: The cumulative 'State of the Answer' and every open question feed next Monday's agenda — research compounds.

nodes.title: Emory verifies facts
nodes.desc: Each claim is checked against its original source. Emory confirms or rejects it — the system cannot verify facts itself.

nodes.title: Verified-facts ledger
nodes.desc: A permanent record of every claim and its status. Events are only ever added, so nothing can be quietly rewritten.

nodes.title: Claim gate (automatic)
nodes.desc: Code looks up every claim in the ledger by exact ID. Unverified ones must be labeled leads; rejected ones are blocked.

nodes.title: Citation check (automatic)
nodes.desc: A checking program opens every cited link to confirm it exists and is reachable; unlinked citations are flagged for Emory.

nodes.title: Integrity officer
nodes.desc: Vets every memo for fabrication, overreach and inflation; objections binding. Trained on the calibration checklist.

nodes.title: Analytics officer
nodes.desc: Ties findings to screened items; source receptivity with copied numbers. Trained on the numbers-of-record rule.

nodes.title: Obsidian archivist
nodes.desc: Keeps the vault's memory current: agent registry, change log, drift audits. Trained on the vault's conventions.

nodes.title: Systems designer
nodes.desc: Builds the machinery: renderers, validators, pipelines — fail-closed, tested. Trained on this repo's guards.

nodes.title: Site experience
nodes.desc: Owns the professor-facing website, the emails and the README. Trained on the site's templates.
